items.prompt: Peeking the minimum in a binary min-heap is?
items.whyRight: The extreme sits at the root.
whyWrong: Log n is for sift after remove/insert.
n log n is building via repeated inserts without heapify care.

items.prompt: Insert into a binary heap is typically?
items.whyRight: Place at the end, bubble toward the root.
whyWrong: Without sift the heap property can break.
Full rebuild is overkill for one insert.

items.prompt: A binary heap is stored as an array because?
items.whyRight: Children of i live at 2i+1 and 2i+2 (0-based).
whyWrong: Hashing is not the heap representation.
Pointer heaps exist but interviews default to arrays.

items.whyRight: n extract-min operations each O(log n), after O(n) heapify.
whyWrong: Linear is not achievable for comparison heap sort.
Log n cannot sort n keys.
Quadratic is naive sorts, not heap sort’s bound.

items.prompt: Priority queue of pending Dijkstra nodes is usually a?
choices: Binary (or better) heap keyed by distance
Unsorted list with no extract-min plan
items.whyRight: You repeatedly need the closest unsettled node.
whyWrong: Unsorted extract-min is linear each time.

items.prompt: Building a heap with bottom-up heapify is?
items.whyRight: Floyd’s method sums geometric sift costs to linear.
whyWrong: Repeated inserts are n log n; heapify is tighter.
Constant time cannot order n elements.
